stem.text: Let f and h be continuous functions with \( \int_{3}^{9} f(x)\,dx = 20 \), \( \int_{6}^{9} f(x)\,dx = 8 \), and \( \int_{6}^{3} h(x)\,dx = -7 \). Find the value of \( \int_{3}^{6} \left(f(x) + 4h(x)\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Reverse the given integral of h: \( \int_{3}^{6} h(x)\,dx = -(-7) = 7 \), and use linearity on the requested integral.

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, one supplied integral runs right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: a linear combination of two functions

distractor_derivations.A: given integral of h from 6 to 3 used as if it ran from 3 to 6
distractor_derivations.C: split written with its limits reversed, taking the integral of f from 3 to 6 as 8 - (20)
distractor_derivations.D: integral of f from 9 to 6 taken as 8 instead of -8
